caveats: CollecTRI/DoRothEA regulons are literature-curated priors, not direct measurements of TF binding or activity in kidney tissue — treat top hits as candidate drivers, not proven mechanism

Small n (6 vs 6) limits power for the per-sample statistical test — report this as a caveat on any TF whose signature-level score is not corroborated per-sample

steps.question: Which transcription factors show the strongest inferred activity change (up or down) between aldosterone-treated and vehicle kidney samples, based on the DESeq2 differential signature?
acceptance_criteria: A human TF-target regulon network (CollecTRI regulon CSV, or DoRothEA human confidence A-C as fallback) is loaded from the reference store and confirmed present before use; report explicitly if absent and stop rather than silently substituting

decoupler's multivariate method (e.g. ulm or consensus) is run on the DESeq2 gene-level statistic (e.g. the Wald stat or log2FC/padj-derived t-statistic) against the regulon to produce one activity score per TF
decoupler is also run per-sample (on normalized/vst expression, 12 samples x genes) against the same regulon to get a TF-by-sample activity matrix

Per-sample TF activity scores are compared between the 6 treated and 6 control samples (t-test or Wilcoxon, BH-corrected) to confirm the direction and statistical consistency of top TFs from the signature-level result
A ranked table of TFs (activity score, direction, per-sample test p-value/padj) is produced, with the top drivers (both up- and down-regulated activity) clearly flagged

steps.question: Do the top TF drivers identified from the regulon-based activity inference have independent support from ChIP-seq-based TF-target binding sets (MSigDB GTRD) and from pathway enrichment of the DESeq2 signature (WikiPathways human)?
acceptance_criteria: MSigDB GTRD TF-target gene sets (unsigned) and WikiPathways human GMT are confirmed present and loaded

Enrichment results for the GTRD TF sets are cross-referenced against the top TFs from T2S1's regulon-based ranking, explicitly noting overlap/agreement or lack thereof (GTRD sets carry no direction, so agreement is limited to identity of the TF, not the sign)
Pathway enrichment results (WikiPathways) are reported alongside the TF list to give biological context (e.g. mineralocorticoid/sodium transport-related pathways expected for aldosterone treatment)
Final output is a consolidated report ranking candidate TF drivers with: signature-level activity score, per-sample directional consistency, and orthogonal GTRD/pathway support

plan.title: TF activity drivers of aldosterone response in kidney
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq (12000 genes x 12 samples, Salmon gene-level counts) with a clean 6 vs 6 unpaired design (aldosterone-treated vs vehicle, single batch). To identify which transcription factors drive the treated-vs-control response, the standard and most defensible route is: (1) run a proper count-based differential expression model (DESeq2) to get a stable, variance-moderated gene-level signature rather than relying on fold-changes computed ad hoc; (2) feed the resulting per-gene statistics into a TF-activity inference method (decoupler with the CollecTRI or DoRothEA human regulon, both present in the reference store) using a multivariate method (e.g. ULM/consensus) to estimate per-TF activity scores from the differential signature, which is the accepted way to answer 'which TFs drive this response' from bulk transcriptomics without direct TF binding data; (3) also compute per-sample TF activity scores (not just on the summary statistic) so the direction and consistency across the 6 vs 6 replicates can be verified statistically (t-test/Wilcoxon on per-sample scores between groups), guarding against a single-contrast artifact; (4) cross-check the top TFs against pathway context (WikiPathways human) and, secondarily, the TF-target sets from MSigDB GTRD (unsigned, ChIP-based) as an orthogonal, non-regulon-model line of evidence, since CollecTRI/DoRothEA regulons are literature-curated priors and an independent binding-based set guards against over-reliance on one resource. All human reference resources needed (CollecTRI regulon, DoRothEA human regulon, WikiPathways human, MSigDB GTRD TF sets) are present in the reference store and organism-matched (Homo sapiens). No translational/clinical steps are warranted since the question is purely mechanistic (TF driver discovery), not biomarker or drug-target evaluation.
